First add $$\upsilon + \chi$$ in vector form: $$\begin{matrix} \left(\ldots , 0 , 0 , 0 , 1 , 1 , 1 , 1 , \ldots\right) \\ + \left(\ldots , 1 , 1 , 1 , 1 , 1 , 1 , 1 , \ldots\right) \\ = \left(\ldots , 1 , 1 , 1 , 2 , 2 , 2 , 2 , \ldots\right)\end{matrix} \uparrow k = 0$$

Then add the terms in the formal description to get a new formal description: $$\upsilon + \chi = \left{Z_{k}\right} , where Z_{k} = u_{k} + c_{k} = \left{\right. 1 + 1 0 + 1 if k \geq 0 if k < 0 = \left{\right. 2 & if k \geq 0 1 & if k < 0$$
Verify that the three conditions for a linear time invariant transformation hold. Specifically, for any two signals $$\{ x_{k}\}$$ and $$\{ y_{k}\}$$ , and scalar $$c$$ , observe that

list.item: $$T \left(\right. \left{\right. x_{k} + y_{k} \left.\right} \left.\right) = \left{\right. 3 \left(\right. x_{k} + y_{k} \left.\right) - 2 \left(\right. x_{k - 1} + y_{k - 1} \left.\right) \left.\right} = \left{\right. 3 x_{k} - 2 x_{k - 1} \left.\right} + \left{\right. 3 y_{k} - 2 y_{k - 1} \left.\right} = T \left(\right. \left{\right. x_{k} \left.\right} \left.\right) + T \left(\right. \left{\right. y_{k} \left.\right} \left.\right)$$

$$T \left(\right. c \left{\right. x_{k} \left.\right} \left.\right) = \left{\right. 3 c x_{k} - 2 c x_{k - 1} \left.\right} = c \left{\right. 3 x_{k} - 2 x_{k - 1} \left.\right} = c T \left(\right. \left{\right. x_{k} \left.\right} \left.\right)$$

problem.paragraph: Thus $$T$$ is a linear time invariant transformation.

To find a vector in the kernel of $$T$$ , set $$T(\{ x_{k}\}) = \{ 3x_{k} - 2x_{k - 1}\} = \{ 0\}$$ . Then for each $$k$$ , notice $$3x_{k} - 2x_{k - 1} = 0$$ and hence $$x_{k} = \frac{2}{3}x_{k - 1}$$ . Picking a nonzero value for $$x_{0}$$ , say $$x_{0} = 1$$ , then $$x_{1} = \frac{2}{3}$$ , $$x_{2} = \left( \frac{2}{3} \right)^{2}$$ , and in general, $$x_{k} = \left( \frac{2}{3} \right)^{k}$$ . To verify that this signal is indeed in the kernel of $$T$$ observe that $$T\left( \left\{ \left( \frac{2}{3} \right)^{k} \right\} \right) = \left\{ {3\left( \frac{2}{3} \right)^{k} - 2\left( \frac{2}{3} \right)^{k - 1}} \right\} = \left\{ {\left( \frac{2}{3} \right)^{k - 1}\left( {3\left( \frac{2}{3} \right) - 2} \right)} \right\} = \left\{ 0 \right\}$$ . Notice that $$\left\{ \left( \frac{2}{3} \right)^{k} \right\}$$ is the exponential signal with $$c = \frac{2}{3}$$ .
